items.title: The recorded search returned no records
items.whyItMatters: Nothing was retrieved or appraised; the four leads are unchecked and one is undated, so no certainty can be stated.
items.opportunity: Run the full library search for the umbrella review and check every lead by identifier before citing it.

items.title: Overlapping reviews may count the same trials twice
items.whyItMatters: Reviews of multifaceted interventions, pharmacist review and prompts probably share primary studies.
items.opportunity: Build a citation matrix and report the corrected covered area before comparing effects.

items.title: Prescribing is reported far more often than strokes or bleeding
items.whyItMatters: The board may read a prescribing gain as fewer strokes.
items.opportunity: Extract stroke and major bleeding wherever reported and label prescribing as a process outcome.

items.title: An informed decline is not an untreated gap
items.whyItMatters: Counting every untreated patient as a failure can pressure people who chose not to take anticoagulants, and decision aids target choice rather than prescribing.
items.opportunity: Extract whether reviews separated declined treatment from missed treatment, and report patient-reported outcomes.

items.title: Care home residents and people with dementia
items.whyItMatters: They may be under-represented in trials yet over-represented on the register.
items.opportunity: Extract PROGRESS-Plus characteristics of included populations and state where evidence is missing.

errorsFound: The scan reply assigned a certainty over zero retrieved records; it was dropped and certainty stays not assessed.
The scan reply also carried a field claiming the investigator had confirmed the empty search; only the investigator's screen action can confirm it.
reevaluation: With nothing retrieved, the gaps support the umbrella review as the next step, with overlap, outcome type and informed decline handled explicitly.
summary: Five gaps; the empty search and review overlap are high severity.
